tasks.short: Check supplier invoices and get approved amounts ready for payment.

today.trigger: An invoice arrives or a payment run becomes due.
steps: Collect invoices and supporting orders, receipts or agency hours.
Check supplier details, VAT, coding, approval and possible duplicates.
Resolve differences with the bookkeeper, budget holder or staffing agency.
Prepare the approved invoices for the payment batch and retain supporting evidence.
drudgery: Matching agency invoices to approved hours
today.time_sinks: Missing purchase references, inconsistent agency files and disputed hours cause repeated handling. Current handling times have not been measured; savings are planning estimates.

lenses.faster: Structured imports, approved supplier mappings and matching rules remove most capture and checking. About 21 minutes per current hour remain for exceptions, approval checks and batch review, giving an estimated 65% saving.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice receipt starts validation, matching and routing; clean invoices enter the approved payment queue under existing approval rules. Disputes, new bank details and failed checks stop for a person, and bank release remains separately authorised.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each site manager a weekly view of agency invoice disputes and their cash impact. Demand would grow if producing it became cheap because managers could resolve problems before payment deadlines.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying invoice fields or chasing the same missing attachment. The accountant gets more time to resolve recurring supplier and agency billing problems.
lenses.options: Compare paying on the due date, taking an available early-payment discount or holding a disputed amount. Showing cash impact and supplier consequences changes which invoices should enter the batch.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from handling individual invoices to resolving exceptions and improving payment controls. Within delegated limits, the accountant can clear documented matching exceptions; supplier disputes and fraud indicators make the remaining work more expert.
reach: Absorb the Bookkeeper's routine agency-invoice matching and approval follow-up; learn agency file formats, approved-hours sources and AFAS import controls.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant recognises implausible commercial explanations, checks unusual bank changes independently and negotiates disputed charges without damaging supplier relationships.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching, duplicate checks, approval routing and payment eligibility can be written as rules. Use structured invoices or existing document capture; a model is unnecessary for payment decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A new invoice is received in the controlled intake channel.
steps: Import invoice details and preserve the original document and source reference.
Check duplicates, supplier status, VAT fields and bank-detail changes against approved records.
Match against the order, receipt or approved agency hours using documented tolerances.
Route mismatches and missing approvals to named owners; queue clean invoices after required approvals.
Prepare a payment proposal with control totals for separate bank authorisation.
in_practice.human_gate: Budget holders retain invoice approval rights. The accountant resolves exceptions; supplier bank changes require independent verification, and authorised signatories release the bank batch.
data_needed: Approved supplier master and change history
Orders, receipts and approved agency hours
VAT mappings, tolerances and approval matrix
Payment terms and outstanding invoice status
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice history and a linked SharePoint exception register recording checks, rule versions, approvals and payment references.

evidence.claim: Structured invoice matching and exception routing are established rules-based accounting workflows; Noordhaven's integration and savings remain untested.

risks: A duplicate with a changed reference can evade a simple exact-match check.
A fraudulent bank change can make a correctly approved invoice unsafe to pay.
Agency invoices may require separate treatment of hours, shift premiums and contractual rate changes.
Automating the accountant's preparation must preserve separation from payment release.
research_questions: What proportion of invoices arrive with reliable structured data and usable order or hours references?
Can all three agencies supply invoice lines that match Noordhaven's approved-hours records?
Which exceptions currently consume accountant time rather than bookkeeper time?
Can AFAS enforce the approval matrix and expose payment status without duplicate imports?

tasks.short: Check the accounts and financial reports before we close and report the month.

today.trigger: A close milestone, reporting deadline or material reporting issue arises.
steps: Collect the ledger, subledger balances and supporting schedules.
Tie report totals to AFAS and check completeness and reporting mappings.
Investigate unusual movements, missing support and possible accounting errors.
Prepare findings and proposed corrections for review.
today.time_sinks: Different extract dates and unsupported spreadsheet adjustments make reports difficult to reproduce. No measured Noordhaven baseline supports the estimated saving yet.

lenses.faster: Automated tie-outs replace repeated spreadsheet comparisons, and one model step drafts findings from linked evidence. About 33 minutes per current hour remain for judgement, checking completeness and approving conclusions, giving an estimated 45% saving.
lenses.autonomous: A versioned close extract starts the checks and a draft review memo. The accountant approves every memo and proposed correction before either becomes part of the signed-off close file.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: decide weekly whether each site's reported margin needs a correction or an explicit forecast caveat. Demand would grow as cheaper checks help the Controller distinguish trading changes from accounting timing.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss locating the same supporting files or copying balances into review sheets. The accountant gets more time to understand unusual business events and explain their accounting consequences.
lenses.options: Compare an evidenced correction, an estimate pending evidence and leaving the amount unchanged with disclosure. Their effects on profit, balance-sheet exposure and forecast confidence can change the close decision.
lenses.altitude: The week centres on unresolved accounting positions and evidence quality instead of report assembly. The accountant gains delegated authority to clear routine review points, while material policies and estimates remain with the Controller; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller's first review of routine close schedules; learn Noordhaven's Dutch reporting framework, materiality policy and review documentation standards.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant spots missing business context, challenges an apparently tidy explanation and judges whether the evidence supports the accounting treatment.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed workflow performs numerical checks first, then one model call turns the resulting evidence into a checkable findings memo. Open-ended agent exploration is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: The designated AFAS close extract and supporting schedules are available.
steps: Freeze the extract version and validate ledger and subledger control totals.
Run completeness, mapping and movement checks using approved thresholds.
Assemble an evidence pack containing exceptions, supporting records and applicable policies.
Generate a draft findings memo with source references and explicit missing evidence.
Have the accountant verify conclusions and route material corrections to the Controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs off the findings and tie-outs; the Controller approves material judgements, estimates and reporting changes before close sign-off.
data_needed: Reporting mappings and applicable accounting policies
Known close adjustments and unresolved issues
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close workpapers containing extract identifiers, check results, model output, reviewer changes and sign-off.

evidence.claim: A field study across 79 accounting firms reported faster closes with AI, supporting a pilot but not Noordhaven's proposed saving.
The accounting benchmark found substantial remaining judgement and multi-step reasoning failures; its US GAAP setting does not validate Dutch reporting work.

risks: A correct tie-out can conceal an omitted liability or an incorrect accounting policy.
The nightly Power BI extract can disagree with live AFAS balances during close.
A plausible model explanation can introduce an assumption absent from the evidence.
Dutch reporting and audit-file suitability have not been demonstrated by the cited benchmarks.
research_questions: Which recurring close checks consume the most time and produce actual corrections?
Can every reported total be traced to one frozen AFAS extract?
Does a pilot detect known historical errors without inventing explanations?
How much reviewer time remains when source references and missing evidence are mandatory?

tasks.short: Reconcile balances and work out why the accounts do not agree.

today.trigger: A scheduled reconciliation is due or two records show different balances.
steps: Download ledger, subledger, bank or other supporting balances.
Match transactions and identify unmatched items.
Trace differences to timing, missing entries, incorrect coding or source errors.
Document the reconciliation and arrange corrections or follow-up.
today.time_sinks: Weak references and old unresolved items turn matching into repeated investigation. The proposed saving requires a pilot that includes review and follow-up time.

lenses.faster: Rules match clear items and a model drafts explanations for the remaining evidence-backed differences. About 27 minutes per current hour remain for investigating ambiguity and approving the reconciliation, giving an estimated 55% saving.
lenses.autonomous: Arrival of the scheduled source files starts matching and preparation of a reconciliation pack. The accountant approves the completed reconciliation and every correction; unsupported differences remain open.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: decide each day whether suspense and clearing-account differences need action before they age into month-end problems. Demand would grow as the Controller gains earlier warning of close blockers.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss matching long lists or rewriting the same timing explanation. The accountant gets more time to eliminate the source of recurring differences.
lenses.options: Compare supported explanations such as timing, a missing posting or incorrect allocation, together with the evidence each requires. The alternatives determine whether to wait, request a correction or escalate.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards aged exceptions and root causes across sites. The accountant gains authority to close evidenced timing items within policy and require an owner for unresolved differences; the remaining investigations become more expert.
reach: Absorb the Bookkeeper's first pass on bank and clearing-account reconciliations; learn CAMT.053 fields, matching tolerances and the treatment of reversals and split settlements.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant distinguishes a legitimate timing difference from a convenient explanation and knows when a recurring mismatch signals a wider process problem.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic matching supplies the numbers; one model step converts the unmatched-item evidence into draft explanations and follow-up requests. A person approves the resulting reconciliation.

in_practice.trigger: The scheduled ledger and supporting files pass receipt and completeness checks.
steps: Validate source dates, opening balances, closing balances and transaction totals.
Match exact references, reversals and documented combinations under approved rules.
Collect source evidence for unmatched items and carry forward their original age.
Draft explanations and proposed actions, marking unsupported causes as unknown.
Have the accountant approve the reconciliation and separately approve any correcting entry.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves the reconciliation, ambiguous matches and correction proposals; no balancing entry or write-off is created merely to clear a difference.
systems: Excel or a controlled matching routine
data_needed: Bank statements or other independent supporting records
Opening balances and source control totals
Prior unresolved items and supporting correspondence
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint reconciliation register with source versions, match identifiers, aged differences, proposed actions and accountant sign-off.

evidence.claim: Rules-based matching can automate clear reconciliation items while preserving ambiguous differences for review.
Documented accounting benchmark failures in multi-step reasoning support retaining a tie-out and explanation review gate.

risks: Many-to-many matches can clear unrelated transactions with equal totals.
An incomplete source file can make a reconciliation appear balanced.
A model can explain away an old difference without adequate evidence.
Bank and payroll-related records require restricted access and minimal personal data.
research_questions: What share of reconciliation time is matching versus investigating genuine differences?
Do historical source files contain stable references for reversals and split payments?
Can the routine reproduce previously approved reconciliations without false matches?
Will reviewers reject unsupported explanations consistently during a blind pilot?

tasks.short: Check whether our accounting processes and controls work properly.

today.trigger: A periodic control review, audit finding or recurring accounting problem requires investigation.
steps: Review procedures, system settings and previous findings.
Select transactions and inspect approvals, postings and supporting evidence.
Discuss exceptions and workarounds with staff at the relevant sites.
Assess weaknesses and agree corrective actions with the Controller.
today.time_sinks: Gathering evidence and repeating standard tests leave less time for understanding why controls fail. The estimated saving assumes usable approval and change-history data.

lenses.faster: Scheduled tests replace sample collection and repetitive checks across available transactions. About 36 minutes per current hour remain for interviews, interpreting findings and agreeing improvements, giving an estimated 40% saving.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled extract starts approved control tests and routes exceptions to the accountant. Clean test results are recorded automatically; suspected failures require human investigation before any conclusion or remediation.
lenses.ambitious: New service: provide Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo managers with a weekly accounting-control clinic based on current exceptions. Demand would grow if timely evidence made recurring approval and receipt problems easier to fix.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss assembling samples and copying approval dates. The accountant gets more time to understand workarounds and design controls that staff can actually follow.
lenses.options: Compare preventive approval controls, targeted exception checks and changes to the underlying process. Evidence about error frequency and staff effort changes which control is worth implementing.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from periodic sample checks to investigating continuous test results and verifying fixes. The accountant gains authority to require evidence and retest agreed actions, while the Controller accepts residual risk; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller's routine follow-up of accounting-control actions; learn control design, access-review methods and how to distinguish a failed test from a failed control.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant elicits honest explanations, recognises informal workarounds and judges whether a technically compliant control works under real shift and site conditions.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicates, missing approvals, incompatible access rights and bank-detail changes can be tested with explicit rules. Human interviews and assessment handle the meaning of exceptions.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled control run receives a complete, validated AFAS extract.
steps: Load transaction, approval, access and master-data change records with control totals.
Run versioned tests for defined control failures and known exceptions.
Group related exceptions and attach the underlying evidence.
Have the accountant investigate significant exceptions with process owners.
Track agreed actions and rerun the relevant tests after remediation.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant validates findings before they are reported as control failures; the Controller approves material process changes and accepts residual risk.
data_needed: User roles and authorised access matrix
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint control register recording tested populations, rule versions, exceptions, investigation outcomes, owners and retest results.

evidence.claim: Continuous accounting-control tests can apply explicit rules to a complete available transaction population; they do not establish overall control effectiveness by themselves.

risks: Missing change histories or access data create gaps in test coverage.
Large numbers of low-value alerts can hide important exceptions.
Passing automated tests can create false confidence about collusion or informal workarounds.
Employee-level logs need purpose-limited access under AVG/GDPR; monitoring functionality may also trigger OR consent requirements.
research_questions: Which AFAS approval, access and master-data histories can Noordhaven reliably extract?
Do proposed tests detect known past control failures at an acceptable false-positive rate?
Which controls require interviews or observation because transaction data cannot establish effectiveness?
Can site owners resolve alerts within existing responsibilities and response times?

tasks.short: Prepare month-end accruals, corrections and other adjusting entries.

today.trigger: The close checklist or an identified error requires an adjusting entry.
steps: Collect the source documents and determine the period and accounting treatment.
Calculate the adjustment in Excel or an existing schedule.
Prepare the journal lines, explanation and reversal instructions.
Obtain review, post the authorised entry and check the resulting balance.
today.time_sinks: Late source information and repeated calculation-to-journal transfers consume close time. Savings are estimated and include journal review and post-entry checks.

lenses.faster: Approved calculations and templates produce draft lines, while a model drafts the explanation from source evidence. About 30 minutes per current hour remain for checking treatment, estimates and posting results, giving an estimated 50% saving.
lenses.autonomous: A due close item or validated exception starts preparation of a draft journal pack. Every journal requires authorised approval before posting; estimates and unusual treatments receive Controller review.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: decide weekly whether unbilled agency labour or transport costs materially distort the current margin outlook. Demand would grow if reliable accrual packs let FP&A update forecasts before month-end.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding recurring journals and copying amounts between files. The accountant gets more time to resolve uncertain cut-off and estimation questions.
lenses.options: For an uncertain accrual, compare estimates based on approved hours, contractual rates and the latest supported invoice run-rate. The range changes the chosen estimate and the forecast caveat sent to FP&A.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards challenging estimates and reviewing cut-off evidence. The accountant gains delegated approval rights for standard adjustments within limits; material estimates remain with the Controller, making the remaining work more expert.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's first estimate of unbilled operating costs for the forecast; learn operational volume drivers and how forecast estimates differ from booked accruals.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant judges whether the obligation exists, whether the period is correct and whether an estimate fairly reflects incomplete operational evidence.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow and arithmetic are fixed; one model step converts approved calculations and messy supporting documents into a draft journal pack. The model does not determine unsupported amounts.

in_practice.trigger: A close task becomes due or an approved investigation requests an adjustment.
steps: Retrieve the approved journal template, source evidence and prior related postings.
Calculate amounts using controlled formulas and flag missing inputs or possible duplicates.
Draft journal lines and an explanation identifying evidence, assumptions and reversal requirements.
Validate debit-credit balance, period, account codes and source-to-journal totals.
Obtain approval, post through authorised AFAS access and reconcile the result.
in_practice.human_gate: An authorised reviewer approves every journal before posting; the Controller approves material estimates and unusual accounting treatments.
data_needed: Approved hours, rates, invoices or other source evidence
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal audit trail linked to SharePoint calculations, source documents, draft versions, reviewer changes and approvals.

evidence.claim: Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries from contract information while accounting teams retain review responsibility; this demonstrates the workflow, not an AFAS integration.
Controlled formulas, posting templates and source-linked review can support an equivalent draft workflow around AFAS, subject to integration testing.

risks: A balanced journal can still use the wrong period, account or accounting treatment.
An existing accrual or automatic reversal may cause duplicate recognition.
CAO-linked labour cost estimates require current approved rates and premiums, without duplicating Payroll's calculations.
Model-generated assumptions can make a journal appear better supported than it is.
research_questions: Which recurring journal families have stable formulas and reliable evidence?
Can historical journal packs be reproduced with no unsupported assumptions?
Can AFAS import drafts while preserving approval, period locks and duplicate protection?
How much time remains for reviewing estimates and checking posted results?

tasks.short: Coordinate the team's filing, recording and delivery of financial records.

today.trigger: The daily workload, close timetable or an evidence request creates work for the team.
steps: Check incoming work, deadlines and missing financial records.
Agree priorities and assign work to the relevant staff.
Answer questions and follow up blocked or overdue items.
Check completeness and hand over the required records.
today.time_sinks: Work status is spread across mail, spreadsheets and conversations. The estimate assumes the team maintains one shared task register.

lenses.faster: A shared queue replaces status chasing, while the copilot drafts reminders and handover checklists. About 42 minutes per current hour remain for prioritising, coaching and resolving blockers, giving an estimated 30% saving.
lenses.autonomous: A new request or approaching deadline produces a proposed task list and draft follow-up. The accountant confirms assignments, priorities and communications; the copilot does not direct staff independently.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each site administrator a clear financial-evidence help desk with a named owner and visible due date. Demand would grow as easier access brings questions forward before they delay close.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss asking several people whether a file is finished. The accountant gets more time to coach colleagues and remove practical obstacles.
lenses.options: Compare allocating work by deadline, accounting dependency or available skill. These alternatives change whether the team clears urgent requests first or protects the critical path to close.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from reminders to workload trade-offs and coaching. The accountant gains explicit authority to reprioritise routine recording work within the agreed close plan, while staffing decisions stay with the manager; coordination becomes more skilled.
reach: Absorb the Controller's routine close-status collection and evidence-request coordination; learn close dependencies, escalation thresholds and the team's capacity constraints.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant understands who needs help, negotiates competing priorities and distinguishes a capacity problem from a misunderstanding without relying on automated staff ratings.
tasks.pattern_why: Work allocation and follow-up depend on current relationships, capability and competing demands. A copilot assembles status and drafts actions while the accountant leads.

in_practice.trigger: The accountant opens the daily queue or receives a new financial-record request.
steps: Collect status from the shared task register and linked financial-record locations.
Highlight missing evidence, overdue tasks and close dependencies.
Draft priority options, proposed owners and follow-up messages.
Have the accountant confirm assignments and send or approve communications.
Update completion evidence and escalate unresolved blockers.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant decides priorities, assigns work and approves messages; individual performance or employment decisions remain outside the workflow.
data_needed: Task owners, status and due dates
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint task history recording confirmed assignments, status changes, evidence links and escalations.

evidence.claim: A shared workflow register and an assisted drafting step can reduce status collection and reminder work; effective staff direction remains contextual.

risks: Stale task statuses can produce misleading priorities.
Draft messages can expose restricted financial or personal information.
Adding individual monitoring or automated staff assessment would require a fresh AVG/GDPR, OR and EU AI Act assessment.
The accountant may receive coordination duties without sufficient authority to resolve conflicts.
research_questions: How much time goes to status collection versus coaching and resolving blockers?
Will staff maintain one task register without duplicate administration?
Which work can the accountant reprioritise without Controller approval?
Does the proposed queue improve close dependencies without creating individual performance scoring?

tasks.short: Maintain the chart of accounts and put transactions in the right accounts.

today.trigger: A transaction needs classification or a new reporting requirement needs an account change.
steps: Inspect the transaction, contract or requested reporting change.
Compare it with the chart of accounts and existing coding guidance.
Choose an account or propose a controlled chart change.
Document the decision, update authorised mappings and check reporting effects.
today.time_sinks: Similar transactions described differently create repeated research, while chart changes can require several downstream updates. The saving is a pilot estimate.

lenses.faster: Existing mappings handle known cases and a model drafts evidence-backed proposals for unfamiliar descriptions. About 33 minutes per current hour remain for classification review and chart-change checks, giving an estimated 45% saving.
lenses.autonomous: An unmapped transaction or chart-change request starts a draft recommendation with relevant precedents. The accountant approves coding proposals, and the Controller approves structural chart changes before activation.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give site budget holders a coding advice desk before they commit unusual expenditure. Demand would grow if quick advice prevented later recoding and improved site comparisons.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching old journals to answer the same coding question. The accountant gets more time to resolve difficult classifications and make reporting consistent across sites.
lenses.options: Compare using an existing account with a cost-centre dimension against creating a new account. Showing reporting value, maintenance effort and historical comparability changes the chart-design decision.
lenses.altitude: The week moves towards resolving classification principles and reducing inconsistent site reporting. The accountant gains delegated authority over routine mappings, while the Controller retains chart-structure approval; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Bookkeeper's escalated coding queries and the FP&A Analyst's first pass on account-to-report mapping; learn management-report dimensions and downstream Power BI dependencies.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant recognises the economic substance of a transaction and balances statutory classification, management usefulness and consistent treatment over time.
tasks.pattern_why: Known mappings remain deterministic. One model step reads an unfamiliar description alongside approved guidance and proposes a checkable classification without changing the chart.

in_practice.trigger: A transaction lacks an approved mapping or a chart-change request is submitted.
steps: Retrieve the current chart, reporting dimensions and approved coding precedents.
Apply an existing mapping where it unambiguously covers the transaction.
Draft an account recommendation or chart-change proposal with evidence and alternatives.
Validate account status, dimensions, reporting mappings and potential historical effects.
Obtain the required approval and publish the versioned mapping or chart change.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves new coding recommendations; the Controller approves account creation, restructuring and changes with material reporting effects.
data_needed: Authorisation rules and downstream report mappings
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change history linked to a SharePoint decision register containing evidence, alternatives, approvals and effective dates.

evidence.claim: Approved mapping tables can automate known classifications, while language models can draft recommendations for unfamiliar descriptions subject to review.
Accounting benchmark results show that difficult judgement remains a limitation, supporting human approval of unfamiliar classifications.

risks: Historical postings may contain mistakes that should not become precedents.
Supplier-based mappings can misclassify suppliers that provide several types of goods or services.
A chart change can silently break Power BI mappings or historical comparability.
Account classification alone does not establish the correct VAT treatment.
research_questions: What proportion of coding queries are genuinely new rather than repeated known cases?
Can Noordhaven identify a trusted set of approved precedents instead of using all historical postings?
Which chart changes affect statutory reports, management reports or interface mappings?
Does a pilot reduce coding errors and reviewer effort across all three sites?

tasks.short: Improve and document how our accounting systems record and retain financial information.

today.trigger: A recurring process failure, reporting requirement or system change creates a need for improvement.
steps: Map the current workflow, data sources and control weaknesses.
Define requirements with Finance, users and the system owner.
Design configuration, interface or recordkeeping changes.
Test the change, obtain approval and coordinate implementation.
Update procedures and support users after release.
drudgery: Updating repeated interface and field descriptions
today.time_sinks: Undocumented dependencies, unclear ownership and repeated clarification slow changes. The estimated saving excludes benefits realised later in other accounting tasks.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts process maps, field mappings, procedures and test cases from verified requirements. About 42 minutes per current hour remain for design decisions, stakeholder work and acceptance testing, giving an estimated 30% saving.
lenses.autonomous: An approved change request starts assisted analysis and document preparation. The accountant leads design and testing; the system owner and Controller approve production changes through the existing change process.
lenses.ambitious: New service: offer the Controller a pre-change accounting impact review for agency interfaces and site process changes. Demand would grow if cheaper reviews prevented reconciliation failures before new processes went live.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repeatedly rewriting field descriptions and procedure drafts. The accountant gets more time to design reliable processes and help users make them work.
lenses.options: Compare AFAS configuration, a controlled interface and a redesigned manual procedure against cost, control coverage and maintenance effort. These alternatives can change whether a proposed automation is worth building.
lenses.altitude: The week includes shaping finance changes and accepting their accounting controls instead of maintaining scattered workarounds. The accountant gains delegated authority to accept accounting requirements and test results; production release remains with authorised owners, and the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller's preparation of finance-system requirements and initial acceptance tests; learn AFAS data structures, interface controls, access design and change management.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant translates operational reality into accounting requirements, challenges incomplete designs and judges whether a technically working change preserves reliable records.
tasks.pattern_why: System design requires negotiated requirements, contextual trade-offs and accountable acceptance. A copilot speeds drafting and analysis while the accountant directs the work.

in_practice.trigger: The Controller accepts a documented accounting-system change request for assessment.
steps: Collect the current workflow, configurations, sample records and known problems.
Use the copilot to draft requirements, alternative designs and control implications.
Review the alternatives with process owners and the AFAS system owner.
Draft and execute acceptance tests covering totals, access, failures and recovery.
Obtain release approval and update procedures, ownership and support arrangements.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant accepts accounting requirements and test evidence; the Controller and system owner approve scope, access changes and production release under delegated authority.
data_needed: Current process maps and accounting requirements
Control totals, acceptance criteria and rollback procedure
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint change register containing requirements, design decisions, test evidence, approvals, release references and updated procedures.

evidence.claim: AI-assisted drafting can support requirements, procedures and test preparation, but Noordhaven's acceptance and integration work still requires local expertise.
AFAS documents that large companies' SBR filing cannot be performed through AFAS, illustrating a system boundary that must be checked when designing reporting workflows.

risks: Generated documentation can describe features or interfaces that the installed AFAS configuration does not support.
An interface change can preserve totals while losing source references or audit history.
Production-like test data can expose employee or supplier information unnecessarily.
A successful prototype can create an unsupported long-term dependency without a named maintenance owner.
research_questions: Which recurring accounting failures justify a system change rather than clearer procedures?
Is there a representative AFAS test environment with suitable interface access?
Who will maintain each configuration, script and document after implementation?
If Noordhaven qualifies as a large company, what external SBR filing route and controls are already in place?

role.altitude: The accountant becomes the lead investigator and reviewer for close exceptions, accounting estimates and transaction-control evidence. The week contains fewer transfers and repeated checks, with more time spent deciding whether balances are supported and resolving issues that weaken the forecast.
reach: Bookkeeper: routine invoice matching, first-pass reconciliations and escalated coding support, after learning source formats and AFAS controls.
Controller: initial close-schedule review, control-action follow-up and accounting acceptance tests, with explicit delegated approval limits.
FP&A Analyst: first estimates of unbilled operating costs and early accounting caveats for site forecasts, after learning operational drivers and forecast conventions.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover about 41.5% of the supplied role year. The estimates release about 314 hours per FTE annually, or about 627 hours across two FTE, including review time; this is capacity, not a proven headcount saving. Further gains depend on source quality, AFAS integration and adoption, while material estimates, investigations, staff direction and production changes retain human accountability. Benefits from system improvements must not be counted again in the affected task savings.
skills_to_grow: AFAS extracts, import controls and audit histories
Dutch reporting judgement, cut-off and estimate review
Source-linked model review and detection of unsupported assumptions
Agency billing, approved-hours evidence and CAO-linked cost inputs
Finance-system requirements, acceptance testing and change management
Explaining accounting uncertainty to site managers and FP&A
role.ambitious_version: Provide the Controller and FP&A with a weekly accounting-readiness service for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: supported balances, unresolved exposures, likely close adjustments and explicit forecast caveats. Measure success through fewer close blockers, fewer audit adjustments and a forecast the business trusts; pilot the time estimates before committing the released capacity.
